aria: Animated recap of the Lakers' 106 to 104 home win over the Kings: Quentin Grimes' step-back 3-pointer with 56 seconds left that broke a 103 to 103 tie, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Luka Doncic's 25 points and 8 assists, the top scorers, how the Lakers won, and Monday's game against the Jazz.

notes: Box score from the Los Angeles Lakers' 106–104 home win over the Sacramento Kings on Nov 20, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with the player lines checked against the Associated Press and Sportando, and game details from the AP (via ABC News and CBS Los Angeles), the Los Angeles Times (via Yahoo Sports), The Sporting Tribune (via Yahoo Sports), Sactown Sports, KMJ 580, basketball.com.au and Ball Exclusives (via Yardbarker). All 106 Los Angeles points and all 104 Sacramento points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (28–26–28–24 to 28–34–22–20) add up to both totals: 62–54 Sacramento at the half and 84–82 Sacramento after three (Los Angeles Times; KMJ). Team totals (free throws 17 of 22 to 9 of 12, offensive rebounds 9–16, steals 8–6), points in the paint (54–50) and the biggest leads (Los Angeles 8, Sacramento 11) are from the Covers.com box score; bench points (34–5) and points off turnovers (20–25) are from Sactown Sports, and the bench points match the box score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Sacramento's biggest lead was 67–56 with 11:09 left in the third quarter (KMJ). Walker Kessler's first 3-pointer of the season early in the fourth put the Lakers ahead 85–84 (The Sporting Tribune; KMJ), and they led 101–93 with 4:50 left (KMJ) before the Kings scored eight straight to tie it on Domantas Sabonis' free throws with 2:32 left (AP). De’Andre Hunter's driving bank shot tied it again at 103 (The Sporting Tribune). Quentin Grimes' step-back three made it 106–103 with 56.3 seconds left (Los Angeles Times). Luka Dončić turned it over with 23 seconds left (AP; Los Angeles Times), Zach LaVine made 1 of 2 free throws to make it 106–104 (Ball Exclusives), Kessler missed two free throws with 5.3 seconds left (Los Angeles Times; AP), and LaVine's pull-up 3 missed off the front rim as time expired (Sactown Sports). Dončić had 25 points and 8 assists; Hunter scored a season-high 30 for Sacramento (AP). The Lakers are 10–1 in their last 11, it was their fifth straight home win over Sacramento, and Austin Reaves (left heel bruise) missed his fourth straight game (AP). The Kings have lost eight straight (AP). The Lakers host Utah on Monday (The Sporting Tribune) and the Kings host Boston on Saturday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Quentin Grimes' step-back 3-pointer off a pass from Matisse Thybulle with 56.3 seconds left in the fourth quarter that broke a 103–103 tie (the Los Angeles Times gives the step-back, the clock and the 106–103 score; basketball.com.au and Ball Exclusives give the pass from Thybulle and the 26-foot distance; the AP gives 57 seconds). It was his only 3-pointer of the game (box score; The Sporting Tribune). Where on the floor it came from isn't confirmed, and the step-back move itself is not drawn: it uses the template's plain pull-up three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Los Angeles Lakers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Quentin Grimes' listed 6-foot-5 and 207 pounds with No. 5 (Wikipedia; Basketball-Reference) and a 6-foot-7.75 wingspan measured at the 2019 draft combine (Hoopsmatic). He is drawn in the Lakers' home white with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
